title: Chapter 15: Salient Features of the Indian Constitution

blocks.content: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the country. It establishes the framework of governance and guarantees rights to citizens. It is known for its detailed structure and for borrowing many provisions from different constitutions of the world.
1. Lengthiest Written Constitution

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India possesses the lengthiest written constitution in the world, synthesized from various global sources.
The Constitution establishes a federal system with strong unitary features and a parliamentary form of government.
It ensures fundamental rights, directive principles of state policy, and an independent integrated judiciary.
It establishes a secular state framework with single citizenship and universal adult franchise for all citizens.

blocks.content: The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world. It originally contained 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. Due to amendments, the number of Articles and Schedules has increased.
2. Sources of the Indian Constitution

cells: Parliamentary system, Rule of law, Cabinet system, Bicameral legislature
Fundamental Rights, Judicial review, Independence of judiciary
Federal system with strong centre, Residuary powers
Concurrent List, Freedom of trade and commerce

blocks.content: 3. Federal System with Unitary Features
• Powers are divided between Union and States.
• The Constitution provides Union List, State List and Concurrent List.
• During emergencies the central government becomes powerful.
4. Parliamentary Form of Government
• Based on the British parliamentary model.
• President is nominal head of state.
• Prime Minister and Council of Ministers exercise real executive powers.
Salient Features of the Indian Constitution
5. Fundamental Rights
The Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights to citizens to ensure liberty, equality and justice.
6. Directive Principles of State Policy
Directive Principles guide the government in making laws and policies to create a welfare state.
7. Independent Judiciary
• Judiciary is independent from the executive.
• Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority.
• It protects Fundamental Rights and the Constitution.
8. Single Citizenship
India provides single citizenship to all its citizens unlike countries like the USA.
9. Secular State
The Constitution declares India a secular state and treats all religions equally.
10. Universal Adult Franchise
Every citizen above 18 years has the right to vote.
11. Emergency Provisions
• National Emergency – Article 352
• State Emergency – Article 356

items: Distinguishing between Federal features (Dual Government, Division of Powers) and Unitary features (Single Citizenship, Integrated Judiciary) is a high-frequency exam topic.
Questions regularly test the specific foreign sources from which key Constitutional features were borrowed.
Emergency Provisions and Universal Adult Franchise details are frequently targeted in SSC questions.

blocks.content: • Financial Emergency – Article 360
SSC / SSC Exam Important Facts
• Indian Constitution adopted on 26 November 1949
• Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950
• Drafting Committee chairman – Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
• Indian Constitution borrowed features from many countries
